purpose: Public-data acquisition result for the v6.25 probe-to-wing phase/speed/modal discriminator. Published/vector-digitized evidence only; not raw DAQ.

sources.title: Wind Tunnel Assessment of a Robust Gust Load Alleviation Controller Designed Using µ-Synthesis
evidence: Figure 23 publishes experimental WRBM magnitude for continuous gusts at 30, 40 and 50 m/s.
The paper states controller tests at 30, 40 and 50 m/s and that eigenmode dynamics change by only 0.5 Hz across those tested speeds.
Table 1 gives identified first flexible eigenfrequency 8.5 Hz for the updated model and a damping correction factor, but not a wind-on damping-ratio series by speed.
The public DLR eLib item links the paper PDF but no raw/synchronized DAQ or supplementary dataset.

figure23_vector_digitization.frequency_coordinate_interpretation: Marker x-coordinate interpreted as Hz because the surrounding experimental prose identifies the 9 coordinate as a 9 Hz gust and the campaign sweep is stated in Hz; the printed Figure-23 axis glyph/unit is internally inconsistent and is not used as sole unit authority.
figure23_vector_digitization.sampling_resolution_comment: At published sample points the open-loop peak occurs at 9 Hz for 30/40/50 m/s. The paper's stated 0.5 Hz total eigenmode change is below the 1 Hz sampling around the peak and cannot be resolved from Figure 23 markers.

panel_40_m_s_completion_v6_27.paper_scope_note: The paper explicitly states that at 40 m/s not all frequency points were tested; the four published markers at coordinates 7,8,9,10 are therefore retained as the complete public panel, not interpolated into missing measurements.

coordinate_unit_policy.surrounding_experimental_prose: gust frequency in Hz and specifically 9 Hz

panel_40_m_s_completion_v6_27.reason: Peak location and local curvature are directly observable from the published WRBM magnitude panel, but without synchronized phase, near-wing gust transfer and same-test modal poles they cannot be uniquely attributed to H2, H4, H5 or any other mechanism.

sources.title: Assessing Sensor-Model-Fusion Technologies on a Flexible Aeroelastic Wing Demonstrator through Wind Tunnel Testing in the DLR Project SAFER²
evidence: A fast-response 5-hole pressure probe is mounted on the tunnel ceiling above the demonstrator to capture inflow characteristics.
Reference modal data were obtained from 2-minute stationary recordings at 20,25,30,35,40,45,50 m/s and analyzed offline; online OMA tracks eigenfrequency and damping.

The SAFER² demonstrator is based on oLAF geometry/structural design but differs in actuators/sensor complement, so its modal records cannot be numerically merged with oLAF Figure-23 WRBM data as the same test article.

required_but_not_publicly_obtained: synchronized W_probe(t) and independently measured W_wing(t) or encounter-plane gust time histories
gust-reference to WRBM complex phase at two or more freestream speeds
same-test-article independent wind-on modal f_n(U) and zeta(U) numerical series or raw records
common time base / trigger metadata linking flow, load and modal records

scientific_consequence.reason: Published multispeed WRBM magnitude is a product of inflow transfer, aeroelastic load transfer and structural dynamics. Without complex probe-to-wing flow transfer and same-test independent modal poles, likelihoods for H2/H4/H5 are not separately identifiable.
scientific_consequence.frontier: Acquire synchronized raw channels from the same test article; do not substitute SAFER² modal results or model-derived near-wing gust.

data_request_minimum_contract.speeds_m_s: at least two; preferably 30,40,50 to match the published oLAF multispeed campaign
data_request_minimum_contract.gust_frequencies_hz: at least 4 per speed spanning the first flexible mode; 5-12 Hz preferred
channels: upstream fast-response 5-hole probe vertical-gust/angle-of-attack time series
independent near-wing or encounter-plane gust time series
WRBM time series on the same clock
independent wind-on accelerometer/modal-identification records sufficient for f_n and zeta
